title: Tech View groups the table by lead technician with a header and count
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in on the Work Orders build under test with Work Orders view permission; the Board View and Tech View display options are on.
  2. The current location has at least 3 lead technicians shown as groups/columns (a technician is eligible when they are Clockable, Active, and their role is not Office or Time Clock User).
  3. Via New Work Order, create several work orders and set a Lead Technician on each, spread across the technicians with some left Unassigned; then open the Work Orders page.
  4. Location has several eligible technicians (Clockable, Active, role not Office / not Time Clock User, enrolled here) and seeded work orders spread across statuses (Estimate, Approved, In Progress, Review/Ready for Review, Complete, Invoiced, Paid, Declined, Imported), including at least one with no lead technician.
  5. In Tech View.
custom_steps:
1. Switch to Tech View.
  2. Observe the grouping and separators between technicians.
  3. Read a group header.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Tech View groups the work-order table under each lead technician, with a visible separator between groups.
  • Each group header shows the technician's name, avatar, and the count of matching work orders.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-10043 (Work Orders — Board View & Tech View Display Options). Story reference: SV-10045 — Tech View. Spec: Confluence page 845185030 “Work Orders — Board View & Tech View Display Options”, PRD v33 (2026-09-28), requirement(s) S2-R1, S2-R12 (read 30 Sep 2026). Review decisions/answers: Confluence page 853901313 where cited. Source-verified on 30 September 2026; not yet build-verified.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S2-R1: “Group work orders by lead technician with visible separators.”
  • S2-R12: “Each group header shows the technician’s name, avatar, and a count of the work orders currently shown in that group, after the filter view and filters are applied, so the count always matches the rows listed.”
